chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, or someone else, from Muhammad ibn Uzafar, from Umar ibn Yazeed who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the charity upon the people of the valleys and the wilderness, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Give charity upon the children, and the women, and the sick, and the weak, and the old'; and he (peace be upon him) had forbidden [giving to] those who are able, meaning the ones with the (earning) capacity.

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الشُّعُور: Those with sense/capacity (idiom for able earners)

ai.seo_question: Who is the primary recipient of charity according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the distribution of sadaqah by prioritizing the vulnerable—children, women, the elderly, and the weak—over 'al-jummaniyyun' (those with sufficient means or livestock), a distinction rooted in the socio-economic realities of early Islamic Iraq. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on targeted charity to ensure resources reach those most in need rather than the self-sufficient, aligning with the broader jurisprudential discussion on the eight categories of recipients in Surah At-Tawbah.
